title: Calm Linen — Notion-Style Documentation Bento
description: A warm-cream, shadow-free bento grid housing four live UI fragments — database table, kanban board, meeting notes, and task checklist — inside hairline-bordered cards. Communicates feature breadth at a glance without resorting to icon grids or marketing copy.
philosophy: This template exists for builders presenting tools to other builders — audiences who read changelogs before signing up and distrust polish that outpaces substance. It refuses drop shadows, vibrant accent floods, and decorative chrome; every element either simulates real UI or gets out of the way. The warm linen ground keeps the technical content approachable without romanticizing it. Restraint here is not minimalism for aesthetics — it is credibility by design.
goodFor: SaaS product landing slides introducing a documentation or workspace tool
Feature overview slides showing 4 distinct UI components side-by-side
Developer- or operator-audience pitch decks where authenticity outweighs spectacle
Investor demos for productivity or knowledge-management startups
avoidFor: Emotionally driven keynotes requiring a single dominant full-bleed visual
Chart-heavy quarterly business reviews where data density matters most
Luxury, fashion, or lifestyle brand presentations
Slides where per-tile copy exceeds 40 words
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide carries the quiet authority of a well-kept internal wiki — purposeful, unhurried, and exactly as finished as it needs to be. Compositional tension lives in the asymmetry between the weighted typographic zone on the left and the airy, grid-ruled ghost cards on the right, implying depth without demonstrating it. The mood is earned credibility: warm but not cozy, structured but not corporate. Avoid decorative gradients, softening glows, drop shadows, and any illustrative element that signals marketing rather than craft.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid; title and subtitle stack left-anchored in cols 1–7 with an 8% outer margin on all edges, creating breathing room without feeling sparse. Cols 8–12 hold a skeletal 2×2 bento card cluster in hairline-only state — no content, just structural presence — acting as a visual counterweight that previews the deck's grammar. Hierarchy is established through scale contrast alone; no rule lines, no color bands, no header strip. A deck identifier or date tag sits bottom-left in subordinate type; no footer bar.

examples.promptCore: The slide feels like opening a well-organized workspace — a warm neutral ground anchors four bento tiles that simulate real product UI rather than decorate it. Asymmetric card sizing drives hierarchy: one dominant wide tile commands attention while three supporting tiles complete the feature story in a dense-modular rhythm. Every surface reads as purposeful and earned; credibility comes from authenticity to actual software interfaces. Avoid gradients, glow, rounded-corner excess, or any visual move that outpaces the substance it surrounds.

Each tile is a hairline-bordered card containing a distinct simulated UI fragment; hierarchy is established by tile size contrast alone — no shadows, no background fills beyond the base linen.
